land.text: Middle Congo, which 'became known as the Republic of the Congo in 1958' (established 28 November 1958 as an autonomous colony within the French Community after French Equatorial Africa was dissolved)

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's French Fifth Republic shape of 1960 (8.47 M km2) still holds the whole country (1,293 grid cells, about 327,000 km2); the Congo's own row starts in 1961. French Equatorial Africa ('organized in 1908') was dissolved into its parts in 1958 (Congo page).

correction.text: the Republic of the Congo as drawn for 1961: the state that 'became fully independent from France on 15 August 1960'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row starts in 1961 but independence was on 15 August 1960; for 1960 Cliopatria draws the country inside the French Fifth Republic shape, whose dossier (eu-22) must give it up.

345,888 km2 against the infobox's 342,000 km2 (no year), ratio 1.01. The page records no border change after independence; the Congo River is the frontier with the other Congo and 'the Angolan exclave of Cabinda' lies to the south. This is not the Democratic Republic of the Congo's shape: the page says the Republic 'is a distinct country'.

region.text: the Republic of the Congo (the former Middle Congo)

ledger.note: 1960-08-15: the Republic of the Congo becomes independent. 'The Republic of the Congo became fully independent from France on 15 August 1960'; Youlou 'became the first President'. The republic had been established as an autonomous colony on 28 November 1958.

1969-12-31: the People's Republic of the Congo is established. Infobox: 'Establishment of the People's Republic of the Congo: 31 December 1969'; Ngouabi proclaimed 'Africa's first people's republic'. No change of territory.

1992-03-15: the People's Republic is disestablished and the state is again the Republic of the Congo, after the introduction of multi-party elections (infobox: 'Disestablishment of the People's Republic: 15 March 1992'). The page does not state the new name in so many words.

region.text: 'several areas in the south of the country' seized by the Ninja and Nsiloulou militias in the last quarter of 1998; Chadian and Angolan forces were deployed to Bouenza, Niari, Lekoumou and the Pool department 'aiming to counter increased rebel activity'

ledger.note: 1998, last quarter: Ninja and Nsiloulou militias seize ground in the south. 'Ninja and Nsiloulou militia seized control of several areas in the south of the country' (the Nsiloulou formed in the Pool department in 1998); on 18 December 1998 Cocoye rebels captured Nkayi, retaken three days later. The page names no district held, so the zone is the four departments it names for the counter-insurgency deployment.

region.text: 'several areas in the south of the country' seized by the Ninja and Nsiloulou militias in the last quarter of 1998; Chadian and Angolan forces were deployed to Bouenza, Niari, Lekoumou and the Pool department 'aiming to counter increased rebel activity'

ledger.note: 1999-12-29: the militias surrender. 'On 29 December 1999, amidst continuous government offensives, a total of 2,000 Ninja and Cocoye rebels surrendered' after a peace agreement that 'officially end[ed] the conflict' (infobox: 5 June 1997 - 29 December 1999, 'Nguesso loyalist victory').

wars.name: Republic of the Congo Civil War (1993-1994)
belligerents: rival political militias (not named on the page)
wars.outcome: 'In the years 1993 and 1994 the first Republic of the Congo Civil War occurred.' No border change.
wars.note: One sentence on the page; no further page was opened for it (budget).

wars.name: Republic of the Congo Civil War (1997-1999)

zones.text: 'several areas in the south of the country' seized by the Ninja and Nsiloulou militias in the last quarter of 1998; Chadian and Angolan forces were deployed to Bouenza, Niari, Lekoumou and the Pool department 'aiming to counter increased rebel activity'

wars.outcome: Sassou Nguesso's victory: Lissouba, who had ordered the Cocoye to detain Sassou on 5 June 1997, was ousted in mid-October; the Cobra militia with 1,000 Angolan troops 'cemented their control' of Brazzaville on 16 October 1997 and Sassou assumed the presidency the next day; the Ninja and Cocoye surrendered on 29 December 1999.
wars.note: Angola 'came to his aid with 2,500 troops in August 1997' and struck Cocoye positions on 11-12 October; the page does not say that Angolan troops held ground or for how long, so no occupation is recorded. The page does not give 15 October for the fall of Brazzaville (the Congo page's 'In October, the Angolan government began an invasion of Congo to install Sassou in power'). Fighting also reached Pointe-Noire, the Moukoukoulou dam (April 1998) and the Pool department.

wars.name: Pool conflict (2002-2003 and 2016-2017)
wars.outcome: 'Fighting restarted in the Pool region' after the 2002 elections and a peace treaty was signed in April 2003; the Ninja rebels 'launched attacks against the army in April 2016' and a ceasefire deal was signed in December 2017. No border change.
wars.note: Two separate episodes (2002-03 and 2016-17) listed as one entry; no ground held is named.

certainty.note: Colonial frontiers: the Congo River with the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the Angolan exclave of Cabinda to the south. The page records no boundary dispute or change; the pages opened give no treaty or survey for the forest frontiers with Gabon, Cameroon and the Central African Republic.

notes: Republic of the Congo (Brazzaville): Cliopatria row 'Republic of the Congo' 1961..2024 (two identical shapes), reviewed with two pages (budget 1-2). (1) Cliopatria gives this row the Wikidata id Q974, which it shares with 'Democratic Republic of the Congo': they are two different states (the Congo page: the Republic 'is a distinct country from the Democratic Republic of the Congo'), so each keeps its own dossier and identity.wikidata is left null here (Q974 is the Democratic Republic's id; the Republic's own id, probably Q971, could not be checked since Wikidata is unreachable). (2) The state is dated from independence on 15 August 1960; the 1960 keyframe is new and the French Fifth Republic shape of 1960 still holds the country (eu-22). (3) The southern contest of 1998-99 rests on a vague sentence ('several areas in the south'); the militias are not a dossier (no ground named, held for about a year). (4) The Congo page dates the People's Republic 31 December 1969 - 15 March 1992 (not 1970 - 1991). (5) The Pool conflict, the 1993-94 war and the coups of 1966 and 1968 are on the page without territorial effect. (6) No ruler list on the page (Youlou first president; Ngouabi assumed the presidency on 31 December 1968, assassinated 18 March 1977); identity.rulers omitted. (7) No gazetteer names were needed.
